title: OpenResty was chosen over a custom daemon, plain nginx and HAProxy because plain nginx cannot read a JSON body and the interesting problems are language-independent
content:
Four strategies were evaluated, and the reasoning transfers beyond this component:

| Approach | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| Custom C daemon | **Rejected for MVP.** Large surface area, long timeline, and the interesting problems — the pinning invariant, the migration story — are *independent of language*. Revisit only if OpenResty is outgrown |
| Plain nginx | **Rejected.** `hash $var consistent` can hash on URL params or headers but **cannot read a JSON request body**, so the path-scoped route would work and `POST /graphql` would not |
| HAProxy + Lua | **Viable.** `http-buffer-request` plus a Lua converter can set a variable for `balance hash <var> consistent`; slightly less mature Lua ecosystem for this shape |
| **OpenResty** | **Chosen.** First-class body access, mature `cjson`, native `hash $var consistent`, rich `lua-resty-*` ecosystem |

What nginx supplies for free is the real argument: the accept loop, HTTP parsing, keep-alive, upstream pooling, **graceful reload** and worker supervision. `worker_processes auto` gives one worker per core, `listen … reuseport` lets the kernel balance accepts, Lua state is per-worker with `lua_shared_dict` for anything shared, and there is no thread pool and no work stealing — each request is handled end to end on the worker that accepted it. "We do not write our own event loop; we do not manage our own thread pool. This is a feature."

The accepted tradeoff is Lua on the hot path: for sub-MB payloads `cjson.decode` costs tens of microseconds, dominated by the network round trip — and the target is LB-added latency in the **low hundreds of microseconds**, regression-checked against a k6 baseline (M0 measured 84 µs median, 172 µs p95). Note the irony worth remembering: body access was the deciding capability, and the shipped header model never uses it.
